about: The technique-Judge test set (SEN-121): drum grip images judged against a Visual brief by pnpm check:technique-judge:live. Correct pairs must pass; deliberately wrong pairs, an image judged against a brief it does not show, must fail. Catalog images are the seed catalog's; the Commons file is the SEN-129 French grip find (CC BY 2.5, Uryah), fetched live. No fist-grip image is in the set yet: none is in the catalog, and one should be added from Commons when found.

cases.name: matched grip in both hands, correct

brief.subject: Both hands holding drumsticks in matched grip, seen from above
mustShow: both hands hold their stick the same way, palms down
each stick is pinched between the pad of the thumb and the first joint of the index finger
the remaining fingers curl loosely around the stick
brief.caption: Matched grip in both hands: each stick is pinched between the thumb and the first joint of the index finger, with the other fingers curled loosely around it.
brief.alt: Close-up of two hands side by side holding drumsticks from above, thumbs along the sticks and index fingers hooked under them.

brief.subject: One hand holding a drumstick in German matched grip over a snare drum, seen from above
mustShow: the palm faces down, knuckles up
the stick is held between the thumb and the index finger
the other fingers wrap under the stick
brief.caption: German matched grip on a snare: palm down, the stick between thumb and index finger, the other fingers wrapped underneath.
brief.alt: Top-down photograph of one hand holding a drumstick over a snare drum head, palm down and knuckles up, the stick angled across the head.

cases.name: traditional grip in the left hand, correct

brief.subject: A left hand holding a drumstick in traditional grip
mustShow: the stick rests in the web between the thumb and the index finger
the hand is turned palm up
the stick passes over the ring finger
brief.caption: Traditional grip, left hand: the stick rests in the web between thumb and index finger, passes over the ring finger, and the hand turns palm up.
brief.alt: One hand holding a drumstick underhand; the stick sits in the thumb's web and crosses the fingers, tip pointing up and to the right.

cases.name: traditional beside matched, each named, correct

brief.subject: Traditional grip in the left hand beside matched grip in the right hand
mustShow: two hands, each holding one stick
the left hand is palm up with the stick cradled between thumb and fingers: traditional grip
the right hand is palm down over its stick: matched grip
brief.caption: Traditional grip in the left hand (the stick rests in the web of the thumb and the palm turns up) beside matched grip in the right hand (palm down).
brief.alt: Two hands on a yellow towel, each holding a drumstick: the left hand palm up with the stick cradled between thumb and fingers, the right hand palm down over its stick.

cases.name: French grip from Commons, correct
cases.note: The SEN-129 live find, not yet looked at by a person: a fail here may be the file, not the Judge.

brief.subject: A right hand holding a drumstick in French grip, the thumb on top
mustShow: the thumb sits on top of the stick
the palm faces inward, sideways, not down
the stick is held between the thumb and the index finger
brief.caption: French grip: the thumb sits on top of the stick and the palm faces inward, so the fingers do the work.
brief.alt: A right hand holding a drumstick with the thumb on top and the palm turned sideways.

cases.name: French grip from Commons judged as German grip

brief.subject: A hand holding a drumstick in German grip, seen from above
mustShow: the palm faces down, knuckles up
the back of the hand is seen from above
the thumb lies along the side of the stick, not on top
brief.caption: German grip: palm down, knuckles up, the thumb along the side of the stick.
brief.alt: A hand seen from above holding a drumstick palm down.

cases.name: fulcrum at the butt end, a subtle wrong brief
cases.note: The photo pinches the sticks a third of the way from the back, with stick showing behind the hand; the brief claims the hand is at the very end.

brief.subject: Both hands holding drumsticks at the very end of each stick
mustShow: each hand grips its stick at the butt, the very back end, so no stick extends behind the hand
the thumb and index finger pinch the stick right at its end
brief.caption: Matched grip with the fulcrum at the butt end of the stick.
brief.alt: Two hands holding drumsticks by their very ends, with no stick showing behind the hands.
